children: Cocoa futures eased to below $6,300 per tonne, extending their retreat from recent one-year highs, amid the dollar strength, profit-taking and signs of improving supplies.
Latest data showed Ivory Coast farmers shipped 2.14 MMT of cocoa to ports through August 30, 19% more than a year earlier.
The country also plans to boost processing capacity to 1.3 MMT in 2026/27 from 650,000 MT. Meanwhile, ICE inventories climbed to a two-year high of 3,411,776 bags as of September 1.

Still, concerns over West African supply persisted, as heavy rainfall left cocoa fields waterlogged and high humidity raised disease risks and weakened pod development, threatening both the current and next crops.
El Niño could add to the pressure by intensifying the region’s dry Harmattan winds.

title: Cocoa Futures Fall
